lawyer:
Md Osman Gani, Advocate ----- For the Petitioner. 
Bashir Ahmed, Assistant Attorney-General ----- For the State.
parties:
HNM Shafiqur Rahman ----- Petitioner
Vs.
State ----- Opposite Party
full_judgment:
Md Moinul Islam Chowdhury J : This Rule was issued at the instance of the petitioner HNM Shafiqur Rahman for quashing the proceeding in GR Case No. 29/2005 arising out of Kotwali PS case No. 29 dated 19-1-2005 under section 409, 467, 471 and 420 of the Penal Code now pending in the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka. 

 2. One Kazi Kabria, Branch Manager of Social Savings & Credit Co-operative Ltd. Bangshal Branch, Dhaka filed a Complaint Petition No. 3035/2004 on 27-12-2004 in the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka alleging inter alia that the accused petitioner was the Branch Manager of Social Savings and Credit Co-operative Ltd. Bangshal Branch, Dhaka at the dates of occurrence i.e. 7-12-2000, 28-1-2001, 31-1-2001, 25-2-2001, 5-12-2004 and 7-12-2004. It is alleged that the accused petitioner himself sanctioned loan in favour of 14 persons amounting to Taka 1,54,700 in violation of the Rule and Regulation of the Co-operative Society. The said loan remained unpaid and now stands to Taka 2,37,785 with interest and the accused petitioner also misappropriated Taka 40,000 from the suspend account of the Co-operative Society. It is stated that the informant contacted with the accused petitioner and also served a legal notice upon the accused claiming payment of Taka 2,43,785 but the accused petitioner never paid the same and, as such, under compulsion the informant filed the case for realisation of the same and also for punishment of the accused under sections 409/467/471/420 of the Penal Code. The learned Metropolitan Magistrate sent the certificate copy treating the same as ejhar and the police vested the same as Kotwali PS case No. 29 dated 19-1-2005. 

 3. The police investigation officer submitted a charge sheet being No. 147 dated 26-3-2005 against the said HNM Shafiqur Rahman under sections 409/467/471/420 of the Penal Code stating the same facts of the ejhar. It is stated that on 17-2-2005 the petitioner voluntarily surrendered before the learned Chief Metropolitan Magistrate and on the same day the learned CMM was pleased to enlarge on bail, to the petitioner accused. It is stated that Md Shahadat Hossain, the present Manager of Social Savings & Credit Co-operative Ltd. Bangshal Branch, earlier filed a petition case being CR No. 947/02 dated 27-4-2002 against the present petitioner for the selfsame allegation and the petitioner with the help of the loanee of the loan repaid the money of the Co-operative Society and on that basis both the parties in the earlier case filed a solenama dated 28-10-2003 (Annexure-E) of this Criminal Miscellaneous case on certain condition. The petitioner complied all the terms and condition of aforesaid solenama and accordingly paid amount of money in cash and also by Bank Pay Order. It is stated that the petitioner joined the Social Savings & Credit Co-operative Ltd as a Junior Officer and subsequently he was promoted to the post of Manager of Bangshal Branch. After certain time he resigned from the said Co-operative Society and joined as Managing Director of Ideal Co-operative Society Ltd. The accused petitioner claimed that the Co-operative Society's claim of the aforesaid money has already been settled and there was no due by the Co-operative Society from the accused petitioner as such the present case is not maintainable under the existing law. 

 5. The learned Advocate further submitted that the instant case was filed by the present Manager of the Social Savings and Credit Co-operative Ltd against the accused petitioner who was the previous Manager of the same Co-operative Society. After more than 2-3 years of the alleged dates of occurrence and also on the basis of self same matter which has been satisfactorily settled between the parties earlier. Therefore, the proceeding in GR case No. 29 of 2005 is not at all maintainable and the instant proceeding is nothing but an abuses of process of Court as such the same is liable to be quashed. 

 7. It is submitted that under sections 43/ 46/49 of the Co-operative Society Act the Registrar or his representative has every power to hold an audit or the Account of the Co-operative Society in each year under section 43 and to submit Audit Report to the Government under section 46 and also to make inquiry under section 49. Under section 83 and section 86 of the Co-operative Society Act debar a Criminal Court from taking cognizance of any offence for violation of any provision of the Act unless a complaint is made by the Registrar or any other person duly authorised by him. The instant case based on no Audit Report/ Inquiry Report or permission of the Registrar but the same filed by a Manager of a Co-operative Society this the proceeding of the instant case is illegal and without jurisdiction for which the same is liable to be quashed by this Hon'ble Court. 

 9. Mr Bashir Ahmed, the learned Assistant Attorney General opposed the rule stating that there are clear evidence that when the accused petitioner was Branch Manager of the Social Savings and Credit Co-operative Ltd, Bangshal Branch, Dhaka during the period of 7-12-2000 to 7-12-2004 illegally sanctioned a loan in favour of 14 persons amounting to Taka 1,54,700 in violation of the rules end regulation of the Co-operative Society which came to the amount of Taka 2,37,785 with interest. Further stated that having required on several occasion the accused petitioner failed to retain the same. 

 11. Having heard both the parties and having peruse the application for Criminal Miscellaneous case and Annexures therein, it is apparent that the petitioner was the Branch Manager of the Social Savings and Credit Co-operative Ltd, Bangshal Branch, Dhaka, has been misappropriated during the dates of occurrence of the offences. The prosecution case is that an amount of Taka 1,54,700 therefore subject to a Criminal Liability, on the other hand, the defence case is that he has repaid the said amount in an earlier proceeding by way of a compromise. 

 14. On consideration of the above facts and circumstance of the instant case we are of the view that the proceeding by the instant informant who has locus standi to file a petition case in relation to the alleged misappropriation of fund of a Society is not maintainable. The learned Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka acted illegally in proceeding with the aforesaid case against the accused petitioner on condition consideration that the case is barred by law as discussed above. In the premises, the initiation of the proceedings is an abuse of process of the Court which is to be quashed.
